title: OneNote: Copilot Chat can create, edit and refine notebook content
summary: Hold: the table presents a web-app Frontier policy API as automation for OneNote preview enrolment without documentation establishing that equivalence. The licensing field asserts an unverified mixed model, and the blanket statements that licensing and permission boundaries are undocumented overlook published Copilot and Frontier rules.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model
claims.claim: OneNote edit mode has a mixed licensing model.
claims.quote: Searched: '"OneNote" "edit mode" Copilot license pricing credits'; opened Microsoft Copilot requirements, License options for Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Copilot overview and Get started with the Microsoft Frontier Program. None establishes a mixed entitlement for this feature.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'per-user' for the documented Frontier entitlement, and replace the notes with: 'For Copilot-related Frontier features, users need a Microsoft Copilot license or a license that includes access to Copilot. The general-availability entitlement for OneNote edit mode is not yet published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/get-started-frontier.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described whose permissions bound edit-mode data access or any applicable identity and permission model.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot presents only data that each individual can access using the same underlying controls for data access used in other Microsoft 365 services. Semantic Index honors the user identity-based access boundary
claims.fix: In Data exposure, replace 'Which data an edit run can read, and under whose permissions, is not described: confirm it before rollout' with 'The edit-mode-specific scope of retrieved data is not described: confirm it before rollout'. Remove the Security & identity bullet beginning 'No identity or permission model'. In Open questions, remove 'and under whose permissions'. These narrower gaps do not deny the published general Copilot permission boundary.
